passages.note: Mathis's No vote on HB2853's House Third Reading rules out rung 5 only; it does not separate rungs 1-4 (direction-only).

passages.provision_quote: Notwithstanding section 15-2401, beginning in the 2022-2023 school year, in this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires, "qualified student" includes a resident of this state who both: 1. Is eligible to enroll in a public school in this state in any of the following: ( a ) A preschool program for children with disabilities. ( b ) A kindergarten program. ( c ) Any of grades one through twelve. 2. Does not otherwise qualify for an Arizona empowerment scholarship account pursuant to this chapter.
passages.note: New section 15-2401.01 extends ESA eligibility to virtually all public-school-eligible residents, matching rung 5's universal-eligibility clause, but Mathis voted No on this single-subject bill.

rows.reasoning: Mathis voted No ("MATHIS N", Passed 31-26-3-0-0) on HB2853 (2022) House Third Reading, a single-subject bill whose new section 15-2401.01 extends ESA eligibility to any resident eligible to enroll in public preschool-disability, kindergarten, or grades 1-12 — matching rung 5's "universal vouchers so that education funding follows the student to any school." A No vote on a single-subject expansion bill rules out rung 5 only and does not separate rungs 1-4, per the annex's own rung 2 note that "a No vote alone is direction-only: it does not separate 1 from 2."
